title: pvNetCDFReader
body:
## pvNetCDFReader

Reads NetCDF files using the CF (and COARDS) conventions into structured VTK data: image data when nothing else is known, or rectilinear or curvilinear grids when CF coordinate metadata describes them; latitude/longitude grids can be shaped as a sphere (SphericalCoordinates). Dimensions chooses which group of variables (those sharing a dimension list) is loaded, and time comes from the CF time coordinate. Use it for climate, weather and ocean gridded data; use pvNetCDFCAMreader, pvNetCDFMPASreader or pvNetCDFPOPreader for those models' specific layouts.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Only variables matching the chosen Dimensions are loaded; set Dimensions when the file mixes grids (e.g. 2-D surface and 3-D level variables).
- Fill values stay as numbers unless ReplaceFillValueWithNan is on, which distorts ranges and averages.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

Native constructor: `NetCDFReader`. Identity: `sources/netCDFReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Dimensions` | Load the grid with the given dimensions. Any arrays that conform to these dimensions will be loaded. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `FileName` | The name of the files to load. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `OutputType` | Specifies the type of data that the reader creates. If Automatic, the reader will use the most appropriate grid type for the data read. Note that not all grid types support all data. A warning is issued if a mismatch occurs. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Automatic","Image","Rectilinear","Structured","Unstructured"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Automatic"` |
| `ReplaceFillValueWithNan` | If on, any float or double variable read that has a _FillValue attribute will have that fill value replaced with a not-a-number (NaN) value. The advantage of setting these to NaN values is that, if implemented properly by the system and careful math operations are used, they can implicitly be ignored by calculations like finding the range of the values. That said, this option should be used with caution as VTK does not fully support NaN values and therefore odd calculations may occur. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `SphericalCoordinates` | If on, then data with latitude/longitude dimensions will be read in as curvilinear data shaped like spherical coordinates. If false, then the data will always be read in Cartesian coordinates. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `VerticalBias` | The bias of the vertical component of spherical coordinates. It is common to write the vertical component with respect to something other than the center of the sphere (for example, the surface). In this case, it might be necessary to scale and/or bias the vertical height. The height will become height*scale + bias. Keep in mind that if the positive attribute of the vertical dimension is down, then the height is negated. The scaling will be adjusted if it results in invalid (negative) vertical values. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `VerticalScale` | The scale of the vertical component of spherical coordinates. It is common to write the vertical component with respect to something other than the center of the sphere (for example, the surface). In this case, it might be necessary to scale and/or bias the vertical height. The height will become height*scale + bias. Keep in mind that if the positive attribute of the vertical dimension is down, then the height is negated. The scaling will be adjusted if it results in invalid (negative) vertical values. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvNetCDFReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
